model: SE7200 Series PIR Ready Zoning Controller
applies_to: Schneider Electric PIR-ready SE7200 series 24 Vac zoning controllers (SE7200C5x45B, SE7200F5x45B).
summary: The SE7200 is a 24 Vac PIR-ready room controller for zoning (on/off or floating outputs). With the BACnet module it is a BACnet MS/TP application specific controller (B-ASC) with about 55 objects: room and outdoor temperature, setpoints, system mode, occupancy, PI demands, output status and configuration objects.
notes: Access comes from the objects table (Present_Value R or R,W). Writable AV, BV and MV objects are marked commandable 'C'.
Group objects (GRP) are listed as type 'Other'; they only bundle related objects. Schneider suggests removing configuration objects from the BAS after setup to cut polling.
State texts and ranges come from the guide's enumeration tables where the object name and instance match; a few enumeration rows use different instances than the objects table and were not applied.
The PIR cover and the humidity sensor are model options: objects marked 'only ...' exist only on the listed part numbers.
Fan Mode, Fan Mode Sequence and Auto Fan are SE7300-only and not listed here; the table still ticks MV 28 Fan Status for the SE7200.

The objects table prints 'General Options 2' as GRP 45, the same instance as 'General Options 1'; the SER7300 table and the configuration section give GRP 55. It is listed once here as GRP 45 General Options 1.

In this table the alarms are BI 36 Window, BI 37 Filter and BI 38 Service Alarm; the enumeration table and GUI list call them BI 35-37. Other slips: the GUI list gives Unoccupied Cool Setpoint as 'AV34' and Output 1 as 'MV28', Figure 1 calls System Mode 'AV16', and the sample program writes occupancy to 'MV13'; the objects table has AV 44, MV 27, MV 16 and MV 18.

source.title: BACnet Integration Manual: PIR Ready SE7200, SE7300 & SER7300 Series (24 Vac zoning, fan coil and line-voltage fan coil controllers)

integration.summary: Command occupancy with MV 18 and the mode with MV 16, and write the occupied setpoints AV 39/AV 40. Read AV 7 room temperature, MV 33 effective occupancy and the PI demands AV 21/AV 22. The BMS can also send outdoor temperature to AV 9.

minimum_points.name: Occupancy Command
minimum_points.why: BMS occupancy: local, occupied or unoccupied

minimum_points.name: Service Alarm
minimum_points.why: Service alarm from an input set to Service

integration.enable: BACnet stays off until the MAC address is changed from the factory 254 to 0-127. MV 18 Occupancy Command: 1 = Local Occupancy, 2 = Occupied, 3 = Unoccupied.
integration.remote_sensors: The BMS can write Outdoor Temperature (AV 9) and, for testing or override, Room Temperature (AV 7); AV 7 only accepts writes while BV 8 Room Temp Override is set to Override. Written room temperature, outdoor temperature and occupancy are released if the controller goes offline.
setup: Controllers ship with MAC address 254, which keeps BACnet communication off. Set the MAC address (0-127) at the controller to enable BACnet MS/TP.
Default Device ID is 72000 + MAC address.
Baud rate auto-detects (9600, 19200, 38400, 76800) at power-up; after a network speed change the device keeps the old speed for 10 minutes unless re-powered.
Default Device Name is the model number plus the MAC address; Device Name and Device ID are writable.
No COV support: poll at 5 seconds or slower and write on change ('if once' or every few minutes), not every program scan.
gotchas: If the controller goes offline, values the BMS wrote to Room Temperature, Outdoor Temperature and Occupancy are released.
Segmented requests and responses are not supported; keep Read Property Multiple requests small.
The device object has no Local_Time or Local_Date, so the controller cannot claim DM-TS-B even though time sync over the network works.
